sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Century Business Media Limited, ISIN INE16VF01010, BSE 544928/CENTURYOOH. Listing 21 September 2026 and allotment 17 September are reproduced in the BSE-notice mirror; official interoperability capital corroborates 8,761,280 shares. Direct BSE PDF retrieval failed. The latest observed secondary close is ₹65 on 15 October, not a live or 19 October price. Review cutoff 20 October 2026. FY26 is standalone Accounting Standards; FY24–25 restated comparatives consolidate the former Railway Media Solutions partnership, dissolved 29 March 2025. All gates remain Conditional. Historical financial confidence is medium; post-IPO funding is lower.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: GOV 5, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 5, CASH 5, BAL 5, EXEC 5 and EARN 6 are supported estimates with counterevidence. BQS 5.46 and GQS 6.55 use canonical weights without a low-cash cap. R is NS; D 4, P 4 and conservative L 1 remain scoreable. IAS coverage and exact bounds are retained without reweighting. L 1 reflects actual recent trading observations and concentration of turnover in earlier sessions, not invented zero-volume days or a suspension claim. Growth is a provisional reported-scope band, not certified organic growth.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Century sells outdoor advertising across airports, railway stations, metro locations and other media, using both digital and static assets. FY26 airport activity contributed 61.52% of sales and railway 24.82%. Management describes five airports and 714 stations, but those counts do not establish occupancy, equivalent economic capacity or owned assets. Concessions require refundable deposits and minimum monthly guarantees, transferring weak-demand risk to the operator. Patna’s new terminal is a growth opportunity with associated cash commitments. The dissolved partnership is historical, not a continuing subsidiary to be assigned incremental future earnings.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Government/transport concessions and an operating network create time-limited access advantages. Tender competition, renewal and advertiser budgets prevent assuming an enduring monopoly. Bright Outdoor’s FY26 standalone sales ₹153.03 crore, PAT ₹24.05 crore, CFO ₹3.61 crore and cash capex ₹0.55 crore illustrate how outdoor-media profits and cash generation can differ. Its advertising/real-estate mix is not identical, so no unadjusted market multiple is imported. Century’s growing airport exposure may improve inventory quality but also concentrates dependence on a smaller set of concession owners and traffic locations.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Earlier DRHP history gives FY23 sales ₹22.5717 crore; latest RHP gives ₹32.0339/₹36.6529/₹46.4334 crore for FY24/FY25/FY26. Reported-scope three-year CAGR is 27.18%; the shorter FY24–26 rate is 20.40%, both within REV 8. FY24’s former partnership contributes only a ₹0.0243 crore loss and negative ₹0.0124 crore net-assets allocation in the consolidation table, but that does not certify an exact parent-only revenue bridge. Scope differences are disclosed rather than ignored. Top-ten customers contributed 45.56% in FY26 versus 39.73% in FY25, so faster growth has not eliminated concentration.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: IPO objects include ₹4.2127 crore media assets, ₹3.7659 crore additional Patna security deposit, ₹1.45 crore debt repayment and ₹3.25 crore working capital. The RHP states that firm orders for all media assets were not placed; equipment quotes and rights awards are not commissioned returns. The Patna first-year average minimum guarantee of ₹40.41 lakh per month annualizes to ₹4.8492 crore. The funded model includes the existing guarantee within operating costs and separately tests incremental escalation/additional guarantees. Deposits remain tied to the concession and are not credited as terminal free cash. Project execution, occupancy and collections must convert the new equity into recurring cash returns.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: FY26 executive remuneration totals ₹0.75 crore; director-related rent totals ₹0.12 crore. March unsecured borrowing ₹4.0646 crore includes director/group funding with disclosed 12% rates. Such support is not free equity and can compete with other creditors. The RHP discloses three issuer cases involving Kancept/Kraft Outdoor with settlement payments completed but court approval still pending at the document date. Separately, it describes State of Bihar v. Ravindra Kumar Chaudhary and Shashi Kumar Chaudhary, C/3156/FIR 82 before the Chief Judicial Magistrate, West Champaran Bettiah, alleging IPC 420/379 violations in a land-related dispute. It states bail was granted and a quashing application 74570/2023 was filed in Patna High Court; the printed hearing date was flagged potentially stale. No subsequent outcome or conviction is inferred. These are issuer disclosures with distinct issuer/promoter scopes, not findings made by this research.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: FY26 restated CFO ₹6.0502 crore includes ₹1.046 crore release of other bank balances. Moving that release to investing gives operating CFO ₹5.0042 crore and CFI− ₹3.268 crore, with net cash unchanged. After ₹2.9822 crore cash capex, FCF proxy is ₹2.022 crore; deducting ₹1.6548 crore additional noncurrent deposits/assets leaves only ₹0.3672 crore before financing interest. The original statutory cash flow classifies short-term borrowing and noncurrent-asset movements differently; its corresponding operating proxy is ₹4.984958 crore, close after small tax/advance restatement differences. No missing-cash allegation follows. Receivables ₹14.158 crore include unbilled ₹3.1207 crore, disputed-considered-good ₹0.8183 crore and doubtful ₹0.2663 crore. Reported KPI EBITDA ₹8.5762 crore adds bank interest only; adding all finance costs gives core EBITDA ₹9.0721 crore. Both conventions are reconstructed explicitly, not mislabeled as unexplained errors. Pledged/margin deposits ₹5.5588 crore are outside free cash.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: At dated ₹65 and 8,761,280 shares, market value is ₹56.95 crore, about 10.25× FY26 PAT. IPO cash is added only once in the pro forma. Issue price ₹74 and 2,312,000 new shares imply ₹17.1088 crore gross proceeds; final expenses are unavailable, so ₹2.5 crore is an explicit estimate tested from ₹1.5 to ₹5 crore. Bear/base/bull growth 3%/12%/20%, margins 16%/19.5%/22% before incremental guarantee escalation, NWC 35%/25%/22% and exit EV/EBITDA 6/9/12 produce conditional terminal prices ₹66.79/₹183.34/₹377.76 and annual returns 0.55%/23.05%/42.19%. Every year links guarantees, taxes, NWC, capex, deposits, earmarked cash, debt and equity. New borrowing incurs half-year interest solved jointly with tax/draws; ordinary repayments occur at year-end. Unverified final fees, deployment and aggregate concession commitments keep R NS despite apparent upside.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Advertising occupancy can fall while guaranteed concession payments remain due. Deposit forfeiture, delayed receivables, unplaced project orders and expensive unsecured funding can then compound the loss. The severe case combines falling demand, 10% pre-escalation margin, 45% NWC, 14% borrowing cost, additional ₹2 crore annual guarantee expense, project cost doubling and disputed/doubtful receivable loss. Separate cases isolate each major assumption, including dilution with no credited proceeds. March RHP contingencies show no issuer GST claim versus ₹0.162 crore previously; separate group-company taxes are not assigned automatically to the listed issuer. Positive cash generation and IPO equity are genuine counterweights, not proof of downside protection.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Fivefold/tenfold equity values from the dated quote are approximately ₹285 crore/₹569 crore. At an illustrative 15× P/E and 12% net margin, required revenue is about ₹158 crore/₹316 crore before debt/cash adjustments, versus ₹46.43 crore now. This requires wider rights access, occupancy and sustained working-capital funding, not merely installing the currently proposed assets. The five-year bull case remains conditional and does not validate a tenfold thesis. Concession renewal/guarantee economics and dilution can absorb much of operating growth before it reaches per-share value.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Obtain final prospectus/allotment financial details and first postlisting utilisation certificate; reconcile net proceeds, fees and debt repayment. Verify asset installation and Patna deposit payment against invoices/bank records. Monitor actual occupancy and minimum-guarantee cash payments, including renewal/escalation terms. Track collection of unbilled, disputed and doubtful balances. Update court statuses from official records before using the RHP’s potentially stale hearing dates. The available secondary history has 17 observations, not 60; observed low×volume median implies 11.36 exit days at 5% participation, while the recent 10 observations imply more than 20 days. October 13–15 each show one 1,600-share lot. Check live depth before assuming the ₹104,000 lot cost makes a ₹5 lakh position practical.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Completed deep review with a conditional investment hold. The revenue record and recent positive operating cash are encouraging, but capital requirements are larger than capex alone and the listed market is thin. Quality factors remain scoreable, while IAS is NS for unresolved expected-return assumptions. No allocation recommendation is made. Reconsider after final IPO deployment, concession cash commitments, collections and execution conditions are verified. Legal disclosures require careful attribution and current status, not a presumption of guilt.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Sources include the September 2026 RHP, older DRHP for FY23 history, August 13 FY26 audited financials posted by the issuer in October, listing-notice mirror and unsuccessful direct-original attempt, official security master and matched secondary OHLCV. Bright Outdoor primary results provide economic comparison. Original statutory cash-flow units/layout and promoter-case page were visually checked. The separate century_funded_model.json includes five annual funding rows per case, terminal-equity bridges, fee/guarantee/WC/capex/loss/dilution sensitivities and solved new-draw interest. Remaining gaps are final issue costs, actual post-IPO cash deployment, full concession schedule, older parent-only revenue bridge, legal updates and market depth. No pending item is represented as a completed verification.

GOV.reason: RPT, debt terms and legal matters are disclosed, and the financial audit opinion is unmodified. Counterevidence: dependence on promoter/related borrowing and court outcomes requiring update limits governance confidence. Disclosed allegations are not convictions, and paid settlements are not treated as unpaid defaults.

MOAT.reason: Concession access to airports and railways supports an established media network. Counterevidence: tender renewals, minimum guarantees and advertiser demand constrain pricing power; site counts alone do not measure usable capacity or monopoly economics.

REV.reason: Reported-scope three-year CAGR27.18% and shorter FY24–26 CAGR20.40% both map8. Older consolidated partnership scope is explicitly separated and materially small in disclosed earnings/net assets, not silently called identical parent history. Counterevidence: growth is concession/customer dependent and longer organic history is not certified.

DUR.reason: Transit/airport traffic and digital/static advertising provide continuing runway. Counterevidence: airport concentration and cash-guaranteed concession costs can prevent sector growth becoming attractive shareholder returns.

CAP.reason: Defined media-asset and airport-deposit objects fund specific expansion. Counterevidence: deposits and working capital absorb much of operating cash, quotations are not placed orders, and incremental returns are unproved.

CASH.reason: FY25/FY26 restated CFO is positive and FY26 remains about5crore after bank-deposit release is separated. Counterevidence: after capex and noncurrent deposit deployment, little cash remains before financing interest; unbilled/disputed balances need collection evidence.

BAL.reason: IPO equity and debt repayment can strengthen the balance sheet, and March cash is separately disclosed. Counterevidence: deposit collateral is unavailable for ordinary spending, unsecured loans cost12%, and final issue costs/postlisting deployment remain unverified.

EXEC.reason: Revenue and cash generation improved as airport activity expanded. Counterevidence: pending asset procurement, new deposit commitments and minimum guarantees mean execution cannot be inferred merely from awarded rights.

EARN.reason: Other income is modest and the two EBITDA conventions can be reconstructed without an unexplained discrepancy. Counterevidence: useful-life estimates, receivable quality and disclosed cash-flow classifications require care; headline CFO is not owner free cash.

R.reason: NS. Conditional baseIRR23.05% depends on postIPO funding, final fees, occupancy and aggregate guaranteed payments. Reasonable fee sensitivities are shown, but these assumptions do not establish an expected return.

D.reason: IPO funding and positive operating cash provide resilience. Counterevidence: fixed concession payments, deposit forfeiture, illiquid shares and doubtful/unbilled collections create credible permanent-loss routes.

P.reason: Dated marketcap56.95crore is about10.25×FY26earnings and may be supported by an expanded postIPO capital base. Counterevidence: proforma book value is not a current liquidation valuation; pledged deposits and specialized media assets may not be freely realizable.

L.reason: Short17-observation history yields about11.36days at5%participation using low×volume bounds, while the recent10-observation median implies more than20days. The latest three observed sessions each trade only one1600-share lot. This supports conservativeL1, not a claim of no trades; no prelisting/missing zeros or automaticG4failure.
